sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this application under Section 438 CrPC, with prayer for pre-arrest bail,
as he is apprehending arrest in connection with South Salmara PS Case No. 15/2024, under Sections 363/343/376(3)/323/ 506/34 IPC, read with Section 4 of the POCSO Act.

3. The allegation against the petitioner is that on 22.01.2024, at about 08:00 am, the minor daughter of the informant, aged about 15 years went to the urinal when the petitioner in connivance with the accused No. 2, named in the FIR kidnapped the victim by gagging her and forcefully taking her away from her house.
The victim was kept confined in the house of the petitioner, who committed sexual assault on the minor victim ceaselessly against her will.
When the victim tried to resist the petitioner the other accused named in the FIR assaulted her with deadly weapons.
The Police was informed who recovered the victim from the petitioner's house.

4. It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that the incident occurred on 22.01.2024, whereas the FIR was lodged on 24.01.2024, which clearly reflects that the FIR has been lodged after a delay of two days and there is every possibility of manipulation of the FIR.
5. It is also submitted that the petitioner is a constable and he was on duty at the time of the incident.
Annexure-C clearly reveals that the petitioner was on duty on the date of Page No.# 3/5 the incident.
6. As the petitioner is booked under a serious offence he is apprehending arrest.
It is submitted that if the petitioner is arrested he will be terminated from service.
7. Learned counsel for the respondent No. 2 has no objection if the petitioner is released on bail.

8. An affidavit has been filed by the informant-respondent No. 2, herein, who has sworn in through the affidavit that subsequently, it was learnt that her daughter was was having a love affair with the petitioner and they expressed their desire to marry each other.
It was mutually agreed by both the families that marriage between the petitioner and the respondent No. 2's daughter will be solemnized, when she attains majority.
Due to misunderstanding and heat of the moment, and as a result of false information about the petitioner, the FIR was hastily lodged.
The respondent No. 2 has no objection if pre- arrest bail is granted to the petitioner.

9. Learned counsel for the petitioner has relied on the decision of Prithvi Raj Chauhan -Vs- Union of India & Others; reported in (2020) 4 SCC 727, wherein it has been observed that- "Concerning the applicability of provisions of section 438 Cr.PC, it shall not apply to the cases under the 1989. Act.

entities.text: Prithvi Raj Chauhan -Vs- Union of India & Others; reported in (2020) 4 SCC 727
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, if the complaint does not make out a prima facie case for applicability of the provisions of the Act of 1989, the bar created by section 18 and 18A (i) shall not apply.
We have Page No.# 4/5 clarified this aspect while deciding the review petitions."

10. Relying on the decision of Prithvi Raj Chauhan's case (supra), it is submitted that if there is no prima facie case for applicability of Section 376(3) of the IPC, the bar for anticipatory bail does not Nashir Uddin Mollah @ Nashir Mollah vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107207153/
2 exist.

entities.text: Nashir Uddin Mollah @ Nashir Mollah vs The State Of Assam And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that indeed there is a bar under Section 438(4) of the CrPC.

It is submitted that if false allegations are leveled against a person, can Section 438(4) of the CrPC be a bar to grant anticipatory bail to an employee, whose arrest will result in termination of his service or suspension from his services.

11. The learned counsel for the petitioner has also relied on the decision of the High Court of Judicature at Kerala, vide order dated 20.09.2023 in Bail Application No. 144/2023 (Crime No.
59/2023 of Vadakkanchery Police Station), wherein it has been observed that- "In the wake of the above findings, the question posed at the beginning of this order is answered negatively.

entities.text: High Court of Judicature at Kerala
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: I hold that the exclusion of pre-arrest bail provision by Section 438(4) of CrPC, in respect of the offences mentioned therein is not to be read as absolute, where it was discernible to the Court that the allegations are patently false or motivated and no prima facie materials exist warranting the arrest of the accused.
The exclusion clause applies only when a prima facie case of commission of offences is made out.
This may have to be determined by the Court concerned in the facts and circumstances of each case."
Page No.# 5/5 12.
I have considered the submissions at the Bar with circumspection.
13. It is true that at present, the informant, who has leveled the said allegations against the petitioner has now retracted her allegations.
14. It appears that the victim and the petitioner are planning to get married when the victim attains majoritry.
However, to consider the bail petition, Case Diary is necessary.

15. Call for the Case Diary and the report if the petitioner was on duty at the time of the incident.
16.

List the matter on 04.03.2024.
17.
Meanwhile, no coercive action be taken till 04.03.2024.
